correctness.rationale: For any compatible metric on the compact product, uniform equivalence with a standard weighted product metric gives a finite coordinate prefix that controls distance at a prescribed scale. A nontrivial coordinate beyond that prefix supplies distinct points which remain equal on the controlling prefix under every group element. Hence their whole orbits remain within the prescribed scale, which directly implies every horofunction is epsilon-non-deterministic. The finite-support expansiveness classification follows from the same obstruction and the standard finite-product argument.
risks: The theorem assumes a compatible metric on a countable compact metrizable product; no claim is made for nonmetrizable uncountable products.
No assertion is made for coupled skew products where equality of a coordinate prefix need not be preserved.

value.rationale: The theorem identifies a sharp structural phase transition for a new 2026 dynamical invariant: finite products may retain directional information, while any countable product with infinitely many nontrivial coordinates collapses the invariant to the entire horofunction boundary at every scale. The same mechanism gives the exact finite-support condition missing from a published countable-product expansiveness theorem. This is a motivated boundary result rather than a routine parameter substitution or finite computation.
risks: The proof is short and elementary; its value lies in the exact structural boundary and literature correction, not technical depth.
The result does not quantify any finer directional invariant after the collapse, because no such direction survives in ND.
